resale_co.name: Continued Certificate of Inspection on Residential Home Resales (resale CO)
resale_co.lead_time: Apply 14 or more business days before settlement for the lowest fee
requirements: House number visible from the street, at least 4 inches tall
Sidewalks safe, no raised or deteriorated concrete
Deteriorated asphalt driveway aprons must be replaced with concrete
Handrails on steps with 3 or more steps (both sides if over 30 inches above grade); spindles no more than 4 inches apart
Porches without perimeter railings must get railings
Peeling or chipping exterior paint scraped and repainted; unpainted surfaces painted
Open splices or improperly installed exterior electrical fixtures corrected
Gutters and downspouts connected and in place
Any other hazardous condition the inspector finds must be corrected
Separate sump pump inspection by the Superintendent of Public Works
Separate smoke and CO detector inspection by the Regional Fire Prevention Alliance (additional fee)

fees.label: Resale CO, request received 14+ business days before settlement
fees.quote: Request for C/O Received 14+ business days prior to settlement - $100.00

fees.label: Resale CO, request received 13 to 6 business days before settlement
fees.quote: Request for C/O Received 13-6 business days prior to settlement - $150.00

fees.label: Resale CO, request received 5 business days or less before settlement
fees.quote: Request for C/O Received 5 business days or less prior to settlement - $200.00

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download and fill out the Application and Checklist for Continued Certificate of Inspection on Residential Home Resales and submit it to the Construction Department at the Borough Municipal Building, 229 Trenton Avenue (856-547-0706; Monday to Thursday 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Friday 8:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.). Also call Public Works (Mike Ciocco, 856-547-2486) to schedule the sump pump inspection and the Regional Fire Prevention Alliance (856-547-0991) for the smoke and CO inspection.
resale_co.contact_title: Construction Official and Building Sub-Code Official

resale_co.notes: Re-checked 2026-10-20: the Construction page and the 2026 application are unchanged. The application is a scanned form with no text layer, so its fee lines were read visually and a text script cannot check them. The web page says the sump pump inspection is included in the $100 inspection (the 14+ day tier); that line is noted here rather than counted as a separate fee. An older 2010 Borough form ($75 initial, $50 re-inspection) is superseded. The page now names Phil Azzari as Construction Official and Building Sub-Code Official (constructionofficial@barringtonboro.com); Albert Hallworth is Building Sub-Code Inspector. Construction inspections are routinely Tuesdays and Thursdays. The Borough also runs a vacant property registration (not a sale item). No town code section for the resale program was found online; validity of the certificate is not stated.

requirements: All smoke alarms (hardwired and battery) must be less than 10 years old; undated alarms must be replaced
Each level needs either a hardwired alarm or a 10-year sealed battery alarm; hardwired alarms must be interconnected
CO alarm within 10 feet of all sleeping areas if the home has a fuel-burning appliance, fireplace or garage; CO alarms must be less than 7 years old
Monitored low-voltage fire alarm systems must be tested by an alarm contractor before the inspection, with a copy of the certification for the inspector
House numbers: Arabic numerals at least 3 inches tall, contrasting, at least 60 inches above ground, visible from the street

Secondary power source label (wording like 'CAUTION MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER', not handwritten) within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter when the home has a generator, solar panels or battery storage
Person over 18 must meet the inspector at the start of the time block

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Alliance smoke detector certification application and email it to firealliance@barringtonboro.com, or print it and drop it in the mailbox at 205 Haines Avenue, Barrington. Include a check or money order payable to 'Regional Fire Prevention Alliance'. Fees are non-refundable. Walk-in office hours are Tuesday to Friday 8 a.m. to 2 p.m.; inspections are scheduled Monday to Friday 9 a.m. to 2 p.m.

evidence.quote: The Regional Fire Prevention Alliance of Barrington, New Jersey serves the Municipalities of Barrington, Hi-Nella, Lawnside, Mt. Ephraim and Oaklyn.
Inspection is required per NJ Fire Code 5:70-2.3 for the selling, renting, or change of occupancy in one or two family homes.
CERTIFICATIONS ARE VALID FOR 6 MONTHS and are Non transferable. FEES ARE NON-REFUNDABLE.
Barrington Borough is the LEA for Hi Nella, Lawnside, Mt Ephraim and Oaklyn Boroughs.

fire_cert.notes: Re-checked 2026-10-20; the Alliance page and form (Nov 2025) are unchanged. The form is titled Certificate of Smoke Alarm and Carbon Monoxide Alarm and Secondary Power Source Identification Label Compliance (CSACMASPSIL). Certificates are valid for 6 months. The form states a $500 per occurrence penalty for change of ownership without the certificate. The form does not require a portable fire extinguisher (consistent with P.L.2025, c.19) but tells applicants to check for recalled extinguishers. The DCA fire directory (survey 9/7/2022) lists Fire Official Nicholas D'Alonzo, 205 Haines Avenue, (856) 547-0991, ndalonzo@barringtonboro.com. The Alliance is run out of Barrington and serves five towns; 'municipal_fire_bureau' is the closest type.
